LESSON: SAUM

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Devotional Acts
Topic 4.3: Saum

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Saum. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are some people exempted from fasting?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. state the categories of people who are exempted from obligatory fast
2. explain the reasons for fidya (compensation) by people exempted from fasting during the month of Ramadhan
3. describe different ways of compensating for missed fasts
4. appreciate Allah (S.W.T.)’s mercy to Muslims for exemption of fasting with valid reasons

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SAUM
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Saum helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: SAUM
Study Saum like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: State the categories of people who are exempted from obligatory fast

What this means
In this part you learn to state the categories of people who are exempted from obligatory fast. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: state the categories of people who are exempted from obligatory fast.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Saum” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can state the categories of people who are exempted from obligatory fast. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain the reasons for fidya (compensation) by people exempted from fasting during the month of Ramadhan

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the reasons for fidya (compensation) by people exempted from fasting during the month of Ramadhan. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the reasons for fidya (compensation) by people exempted from fasting during the month of Ramadhan.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Saum in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the reasons for fidya (compensation) by people exempted from fasting during the month of Ramadhan. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe different ways of compensating for missed fasts

What this means
In this part you learn to describe different ways of compensating for missed fasts. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe different ways of compensating for missed fasts.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe different ways of compensating for missed fasts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate Allah (S.W.T.)’s mercy to Muslims for exemption of fasting with valid reasons

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate Allah (S.W.T.)’s mercy to Muslims for exemption of fasting with valid reasons. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate Allah (S.W.T.)’s mercy to Muslims for exemption of fasting with valid reasons.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Saum” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate Allah (S.W.T.)’s mercy to Muslims for exemption of fasting with valid reasons. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Saum is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Saum” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: state the categories of people who are exempted from obligatory fast)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Saum in your own words. (skill: explain the reasons for fidya (compensation) by people exempted from fasting during the month of Ramadhan)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: describe different ways of compensating for missed fasts)

Example 4: Show how “Saum” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: appreciate Allah (S.W.T.)’s mercy to Muslims for exemption of fasting with valid reasons)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Saum to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: state the categories of people who are exempted from obligatory fast.
3. Practise this skill: explain the reasons for fidya (compensation) by people exempted from fasting during the month of Ramadhan.
4. Practise this skill: describe different ways of compensating for missed fasts.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Saum from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Saum: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Saum?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are some people exempted from fasting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Saum means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: state the categories of people who are exempted from obligatory fast.
5. Be able to: explain the reasons for fidya (compensation) by people exempted from fasting during the month of Ramadhan.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
